$f(x)=|x+2|+1$ is a translated absolute value graph: it has no breaks, so it is continuous everywhere.

It has a sharp corner at $x=-2$, so it is not differentiable at $x=-2$ (i.e. not differentiable for every value of $x$).

$\therefore D$

$f(-x)=\ln\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)=\ln\dfrac{(x^2+1)-x^2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}+x}=-\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)=-f(x)$, so $f$ is odd.

$x+\sqrt{x^2+1}$ is increasing, so $f$ is increasing and therefore one-to-one.

$\therefore D$

solutions.latex:
Method 1:

$\text{LHS}=\dfrac{\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}+\dfrac{1}{\sin x}}{\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}+\dfrac{\sin x}{1}}=\dfrac{\cos x(\cos x+1)}{\sin^2 x+\sin^2 x\cos x}=\dfrac{\cos x(1+\cos x)}{\sin^2 x(1+\cos x)}$

$=\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin x}=\cot x\operatorname{cosec}x=\text{RHS}$

Method 2:

$\text{LHS}=\left(\dfrac{1}{\tan x}+\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\right)\times\dfrac{1}{\tan x+\sin x}=\dfrac{\sin x+\tan x}{\tan x\sin x}\times\dfrac{1}{\tan x+\sin x}=\dfrac{1}{\tan x}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin x}=\cot x\operatorname{cosec}x=\text{RHS}$
